There is a particular hour before dawn when the world seems to hold its breath. The streetlights outside my window cast a soft amber glow on the empty pavement, and the only sound is the hum of the refrigerator, steady as a heartbeat. I have always loved this time, not because I am productive, but because it asks nothing of me. The phone is dark, the inbox silent, and for a little while I can simply exist without performing.

I think we underestimate the value of such unclaimed moments. We spend so much of our lives rushing toward the next obligation, the next notification, the next version of ourselves. But in the quiet, there is room to remember that we are not machines.

This morning, I sat by the window with a cup of tea and watched the sky change from charcoal to pale blue. A bird began to sing, then another, until the whole neighborhood seemed to wake in layers. It struck me that none of this required my attention or approval. The day would arrive whether I was ready or not. There is something comforting in that inevitability, a reminder that the world is larger than my worries.

Perhaps that is why I write. Not to capture the moment, but to sit inside it longer. To turn the ordinary into something I can hold. And then, when the sun is up and the demands begin, I can carry that quiet with me like a stone in my pocket.
